messages:
sre-alex: 🚨 APAC cluster-3 (nodepool: gpu-burst) is experiencing mass GPU pod evictions and autoscaler flapping. Dashboards show a big spike in pod restarts starting ~23:02 UTC. Investigating now.
eng-oncall-lee: Jumping in — many nodes in nodepool are NotReady, kubelet heartbeat lost, device-plugin reporting timeouts. A bunch of pods stuck Pending with FailedScheduling + FailedAttach messages.
eng-infra-john: Observing BGP/CNI churn on the node subnet in apac-a. ARP table size on the border routers spiked then flapped routes between AZs for ~4m. Could be network partition between hosts.
eng-runtime-maya: We had a nightly eval flood at 23:00 UTC — ~120 GPU jobs launched across the cluster. They all target the gpu-burst pool. Scheduling pressure matches the eval start.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler event: scale-up request for 12 nodes triggered at 23:03:10 UTC. Provisioning started. Some instances failed to join; scale-down disabled while incident active.
eng-oncall-lee: Pasting a representative kubectl describe for a stuck pod:
```
Name:         gpu-eval-7f8d
Namespace:    evals
Status:       Pending
Conditions:   PodScheduled=False
Events:
  23:02:35   Warning  FailedScheduling  0/12 nodes are available: 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 4 node(s) weren't ready, 2 VolumeBinding failed.
  23:03:05   Warning  FailedAttachVolume  attach failed for volume "gpu-dev" : device plugin timeout
```
infra-tina: Cloud provider reports some instances in apac-a failed boot due to kernel oops in the custom image. They returned 500s from metadata service during init so kubelet never started on those nodes. Ticket opened with infra-support: INC-APAC-4342.
devex-sam: Customer-facing metrics: a small set of production endpoints in APAC saw 429s and increased latency — likely routing to unhealthy nodes. I'm drafting a short status blurb for customers.
product-jess: Any chance this is related to the new autoscaler tuning we rolled last week? Could be triggering over-provisioning then churning.
eng-infra-john: Autoscaler config change may have contributed to faster scale-up, but root seems to be network/host boot failures. Scale-up created more instances that couldn't join -> more scheduling pressure -> more pods queued -> autoscaler continued trying. Feedback loop.
bot-deploy: Deploy event: nightly-evals v2 triggered 2026-11-03T23:00:00Z (sha: a1b2c3).
eng-runtime-maya: We can throttle evals quickly: disabling the eval cron is the fastest mitigation. Also want to mark eval jobs as BestEffort to allow eviction.
eng-oncall-lee: Mitigation steps applied: 1) Disabled nightly-evals cron (done). 2) Adjusted cluster-autoscaler maxNodes temporarily +20 to reduce flapping (done). 3) Tainted new nodes with gpu-join-unsafe=true:NoSchedule to stop scheduling until node joins healthy (in progress).
infra-tina: Draining the obviously NotReady nodes now to reduce ARP churn. Doing cordon + drain with --ignore-daemonsets, forcible when needed.
cluster-autoscaler-bot: Note: scale-up in progress suppressed until 23:08:10 UTC to avoid oscillation.
eng-infra-john: Quick workaround for the kernel image: rolling back to previous AMI for new nodes in apac-a. That should stop further failed boots. Rolling now; cloud provider ETA ~5m.
devex-sam: Customer update ready: "We are mitigating an infrastructure issue affecting GPU-backed workloads in APAC. Some jobs may be delayed. Engineers have suspended scheduled evals and are working on node reprovisioning." Want me to send?
product-jess: Send. Add a note: teams can fallback to dedicated capacity if they have it.
sre-alex: Plan summary and owners: 1) Stop evals (maya) :white_check_mark:. 2) Rollback AMI for new nodes (john/infra-tina) :in_progress:. 3) Drain/cordon NotReady nodes (lee) :in_progress:. 4) Throttle autoscaler and add taint to new nodes (lee/john) :in_progress:. 5) Customer comms (sam) :white_check_mark:. 6) Cloud provider ticket monitored (tina) :in_progress:. 7) Postmortem to follow, include eval throttling policy and autoscaler guard rails (alex/jess).
eng-runtime-maya: After AMI rollback we should re-run a small canary of 3 eval jobs to validate scheduling before re-enabling cron.
infra-tina: Cloud provider confirms AMI rollback completed at 23:07:50 UTC, new instances booting successfully. Kubelets joining as Ready.
eng-oncall-lee: Nodes are becoming Ready, device-plugin health OK, pending pods are being scheduled. I'll untaint a subset once stable.
sre-alex: Current status at 23:10 UTC: cluster stabilizing, scale activity subsiding, queued pods draining. Keeping incident open until 00:00 UTC for monitoring. Good job team.
product-jess: Please add action item: add autoscaler stabilization window and a hard cap on concurrent scale-up in apac region.
sre-alex: Added to incident tasks. Postmortem owner: alex. Closing updates will be posted shortly. :thumbsup:
